assertions.title: Quote grows with the queue ahead
assertions.evidence: t3-summary.json; t3-queue-before.json (live queue: only the 2 seeded entries were active: wl_acme_1 P2 waiting quoted 20 pos 1, wl_acme_2 P4 waiting quoted 35 pos 2); t3-quote-q0/q1/q2/q3.json; t3-create-a/b/c/d.json (POST /operator/reservations/book/waitlist/ -> HTTP 201 x3 for A,B,C plus D); t3-leave-A/B/C.txt (POST /:id/status -> 200 x3); t3-sqlite-quotes.txt (rsv_waitlist_entries quoted_min A=1, B=105, C=105, D=1). Test used partySize 3, areaId=area_acme_main, where only M3 (2-4) and M4 (2-4) fit. A quoted 1 = standalone /quote 1 (pos 3); B quoted 105 = standalone 105 (pos 4); C quoted 105 = standalone 105 (pos 5) -> third (105) > first (1). After A,B,C were set to left, D quoted 1 = standalone 1 (pos 3) < C's 105.
assertions.notes: Each entry's quoted_min equals the standalone /quote result taken immediately before creation, when the live queue ahead of the new party is exactly the entries ahead of it; positions matched too (3/4/5/3). The direction (third > first) holds because party size 3 in the Main Dining Room has exactly two fitting single tables, so A and B consume both and C waits a full turn (105 = 90 min turn + 15 min buffer).
assertions.limitations: The two seeded entries (wl_acme_1 Julian Mercer, wl_acme_2 Fatima Al-Qahtani) stayed active and were not modified, so the shared queue was never literally empty of every party; 'emptied' here means my three entries were all left and the quote fell to 1. The pre-create /quote and the POST are separate requests; no other validator changed the queue between them in any of the four pairs (quote and position matched each time).

assertions.title: No response by the deadline becomes no_response
assertions.evidence: t5-settings-set-1.json (PUT waitlist settings -> waitlistResponseMin 1, version 44); t5-entry-y2.json + t5-notify-y2.json (operator walk-in Y2 notified, deadline = notified+60000); t5-pre-tick-status.txt (Y2 status notified, deadline_passed=1 at 1792240417801); t5-tick-y2.json (POST /api/reservations/tick -> HTTP 200, task waitlist_offers count=1); t5-y2-post-tick.txt (Y2 no_response); t5-z-onmyway.json (guest POST /reservations/waitlist/status/on-my-way -> 200, status on_the_way before deadline); t5-post-tick-status.txt and t5-y2-post-tick.txt (Z still on_the_way after the sweeps); t5-operator-list-final.json (operator list: Y, Y2, W, W2, X no_response; Z on_the_way); t5-settings-after-restore.json (min back to 10).
assertions.notes: The first Y attempt was swept by the automatic 120 s Node interval tick before my manual tick (my tick reported count 0; row already no_response) - retried with Y2 timed ~1.2 s after its deadline: still notified at the pre-check, my tick reported waitlist_offers count=1, and the row became no_response. Z was notified, answered on-my-way before its deadline, and was untouched by both the interval tick and the manual tick.
assertions.limitations: Attribution of Y2's move to the manual tick relies on the pre-check showing it still notified 1.2 s before the tick and the tick's waitlist_offers count=1; a concurrent interval tick inside that ~1 s window would be indistinguishable, but the timing makes it the manual tick. The settings screen's PUT was exercised through the same tenant-api route the screen calls (contract tool: curl).

assertions.title: Join confirmation message
assertions.evidence: t12-join.json (POST /reservations/waitlist/join, US, phone +15555550801 + email rsv-g8-1@example.com + smsOptIn, -> HTTP 201; statusToken redacted, 104 chars, prefix rsv_w_); t12-email-redacted.json (captured email to rsv-g8-1@example.com, subject 'You are on the waitlist at Downtown Flagship', text 'Estimated wait: 1 min', link http://localhost:3001/reserve/waitlist#t=<status-token> with the fragment token equal to the response statusToken); t12-sms-redacted.txt ([SMS MOCK] To: +15555550801 line with the restaurant name, 'Estimated wait 1 min' and the same #t= status link); final-my-messages.txt (rsv_messages: exactly one waitlist_joined email row + one waitlist_joined sms row for the entry, both status sent; zero rows for every walk-in entry without contact details: A,B,C,D,X,Y,Y2,W,W2).
assertions.notes: Delivery was immediate after commit (sent_at within the join request), no tick needed. The walk-in entries added by the operator with no contact details produced no message rows and no error.
assertions.limitations: With both an opted-in US phone and an email the system writes one rsv_messages row per channel (2 rows for the entry), matching channelsFor (email when email provided; sms only when US + smsOptIn). The contract's evidence note 'one row per entry' is satisfied per channel; there were no duplicate rows for the same channel and no second send after later ticks. The message link points at the App origin (http://localhost:3001/reserve/waitlist#t=...) - the already-reported cross-origin link issue, not re-diagnosed here.

assertions.title: Join idempotency and rate limits
assertions.evidence: t22-idem-first.json + t22-idem-replay.json (same Idempotency-Key g8-22-idem and identical body -> both HTTP 201, same entry id wle_385f41d1..., same statusToken); sqlite: 1 rsv_waitlist_entries row for +15555550802 and 1 rsv_idempotency_keys row (scope waitlist_join); t22-idem-conflict.json (same key, changed name -> HTTP 409 idempotency_conflict); t22-join-burst.json (6 rapid distinct joins from X-Forwarded-For 10.8.3.1 -> 201,201,201,201,201,429) and t22-join-429-headers.txt (HTTP/1.1 429, retry-after: 600); t22-notifyme-first/replay.json (same request id nfy_dbb8362f... and same cancelToken), t22-notifyme-conflict.json (409 idempotency_conflict), t22-notifyme-burst.json (6 rapid distinct notify-me from 10.8.5.1 -> 201 x5, 429 x1); sqlite rsv_notify_requests (5 burst rows + 1 idempotent row), rsv_rate_counters (waitlist_join_ip 5 for 10.8.3.1).
assertions.notes: The 5/10 min limit is enforced both in memory and durably (rsv_rate_counters); the 6th request was refused by the in-memory gate with 429 rate_limited before doing any work. Rate-limit budgets were isolated per sub-test with private X-Forwarded-For identities so no other validator's budget was consumed.

assertions.title: Waitlist offers are also swept inside the write path
assertions.evidence: t23-entry-w2.json + t23-notify-w2.json (walk-in W2 notified, deadline 1792240616782); t23-w2-pre-write.txt (status notified, deadline_passed=1, read at 1792240617988); t23-booking-w2.json (unrelated host booking POST /operator/reservations/book/reservations -> HTTP 201, reservation rsv_3e625f37-e0bd-4c28-b5ad-a76a1089bf09 / code T3BSFV on 2026-10-27 12:30); t23-w2-post-write.txt (W2 no_response at 1792240618116, ~130 ms after the booking); no tick was run between.
assertions.notes: The write path's sweepExpiredInTx moved the overdue entry inside the booking transaction. An earlier attempt with entry W was swept by the automatic 120 s interval tick before my booking write landed (W was already no_response at the pre-check), so the test was repeated with W2 and a tight pre-check/write/post-check sequence.
assertions.limitations: A coincident interval tick inside the ~130 ms window between the pre-check and the booking cannot be fully excluded, but the timing and the 120 s cadence make the booking write the mover; W2 was still notified immediately before the booking.

assertions.title: Operator notify requires its deadline to come from settings
assertions.evidence: t25-waitlist-settings-before.json (GET waitlist settings: waitlistResponseMin 10, version 41); t25-settings-set-2.json (PUT waitlistResponseMin=2, expectedVersion 41 -> 200, version 42); t25-entry-x.json + t25-notify-x.json (fresh entry X notified: notifiedAt 1792240244888, responseDeadlineAt 1792240364888, delta exactly 120000 ms = 2 min; notify HTTP 200); t25-sqlite-delta.txt (same delta in rsv_waitlist_entries); t25-settings-restore.json (PUT waitlistResponseMin=10 -> 200, version 43). Baseline re-verified after the 005 window: t5-settings-after-restore.json and t5-sqlite-restored.txt (waitlist_response_min 10, waitlist_max_parties null, version 47).
assertions.notes: Deadline arithmetic uses the live location setting, not a constant: with the setting at 2 the delta was exactly 120000 ms (a constant 10 would have given 600000). Setting changed and restored through the same tenant-api waitlist-settings route the settings screen calls.
assertions.limitations: None. The extra version bumps between my PUTs (42->46) came from other validators' concurrent settings writes; my restore used the fresh expectedVersion and succeeded.

frictions.description: The automatic Node reservations interval tick (120 s) raced two deadline-based checks: Y (VAL-WAIT-005) was moved to no_response before my manual tick, and W (VAL-WAIT-023) before my booking write. Not documented as a hazard for short-deadline sweeps.
frictions.resolution: Repeated both with fresh entries and tight timing (pre-check ~1 s after the deadline, immediate tick/write) so the pre-state was captured as notified and the sweep was attributable.

frictions.description: The operator create-booking route parses its own body (date/businessDate + time or localStartMin), not the exported operatorCreateReservationSchema (slotMin); first attempt answered 400 missing_time.
